title: A Good Catch Day
logline: One boat comes in low in the water with the best catch of the month; the others come in light. What happens on the sand in the next ten minutes says more than the weighing scale does.

object.note: Object 6 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: From an honest scale at a weekly market to the weighing on a fishing beach, where one boat's big catch meets the others' light ones and the next ten minutes say more than the scale.

thread_out.thread: The softening that lets someone be glad at another's luck becomes a literal one: a drum-maker working a stiff hide with oil and water for days until it can sound.

requirements: A working fishing harbour with multiple crews returning at the same time
A morning where catches are genuinely uneven, not arranged
Crews willing to be filmed and to speak honestly

lesson.in_simple_terms: When someone else has a lucky day, a person can feel pinched by it or genuinely glad. The texts name that gladness as a quality of its own, the opposite of envy, meant to reach anyone who is doing well.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: අනුන්ට වාසනාවන්ත දවසක් උදා වූ විට ඊර්ෂ්‍යාව වෙනුවට හටගන්නා අවංක සතුට 'මුදිතාව' ලෙස හැඳින්වෙන අතර, එය ඕනෑම කෙනෙකු වෙත පැතිරිය යුතු ගුණයක් ලෙස දැක්වේ.
lesson.the_teaching: Sympathetic joy (muditā) is one of the four sublime abidings. The Pradeepika defines it as gladness at others' success, whose function is not envying and which settles discontent, and it warns of a look-alike: worldly, giddy excitement. These abidings are called 'immeasurable' because they are not measured out to one being or one place but are meant to extend to all. The Margaya frames it through self-comparison: be glad at another's gain as you are glad at your own.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: One boat comes in low in the water and the others come in light, and the scale gives its number. The film then stays on the next ten minutes: who walks over to help unload or congratulate, who keeps to their own nets, and whether tea or fish is shared afterward. The viewer reads gladness, or its absence, in hands and faces rather than in anything said.

key_terms.en: sympathetic joy, gladness at others' success
the immeasurables, extended to all beings without limit

lesson.caution: This does not mean gladness for others is simply a warm mood that appears on its own; the texts describe it as a disciplined practice, widened step by step toward everyone.
lesson.builds_on: Fair Measure showed goodness as refusing a wrong; this film shows goodness as a response to someone else's good fortune, where the test is not what one does but what one feels.
